target.title: fix(android): stop push-to-talk from dropping speech after mid-hold pauses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android push-to-talk silently loses speech. The SpeechRecognizer PTT path runs a single recognizer session with a ~2.5 s complete-silence window, `lastTranscript` is replace-only, and the restart machinery is disabled during PTT. Consequences in a manual hold: pause mid-sentence and keep talking — everything after the recognizer's mid-hold finalization is dropped; speak two utterances — only the last final survives.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture is rebuilt as an ordered, closed rung ladder with multi-segment accumulation:

- **API 33+ raw-audio segmented** (preferred): an app-owned 16 kHz mono `AudioRecord` pumped through a `ParcelFileDescriptor` pipe into the recognizer via `EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE` + `EXTRA_SEGMENTED_SESSION`; `onSegmentResults` accumulates finals and the session re-arms without teardown. Input level meters from our own PCM (RMS) since `onRmsChanged` may never fire here.
- **API 33+ silence-keyed segmented**: same segment callbacks without app audio, used when raw setup fails.
- **Restart-during-hold** (below API 33 / final fallback): when a final arrives while the hold is still active, it goes into the accumulator and listening restarts — this alone fixes the dropped-speech bug on older devices.

Failed holds only descend the ladder; the speech locale (`EXTRA_LANGUAGE`) is preserved on every rung. On release, the merged transcript joins finals in order (locale-aware — no ASCII separators injected after CJK/Arabic terminal punctuation) and appends the trailing live partial unless it duplicates the last final.

The release/lifecycle semantics were the hard part and are all regression-tested: one bounded grace waits for the *terminal* recognizer callback so late finals aren't truncated (segments arriving during release accumulate without ending the wait); rapid re-press drains the prior release instead of cancelling it, so the first stop still returns its transcript; cancellation mid-release (gateway drop) tears capture down under `NonCancellable`, resumes realtime talk capture, and resolves the stop payload; callback listeners are bound to their capture id so retired sessions can't mutate the next hold; raw-rung release also calls `stopListening()` because `EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE` is optional and a service may legally ignore the pipe and run its own microphone.

The Live/realtime relay path is untouched — this only affects the node-invoked SpeechRecognizer PTT path.

## User Impact

Hold-to-talk stops eating speech after pauses; multi-sentence holds arrive complete; CJK/Arabic transcripts keep their punctuation; the level meter works on the raw-audio path; releases stay snappy (terminal callbacks normally arrive in well under a second — the 5 s bound only caps pathological recognizers, favoring complete transcripts over silent truncation).

## Evidence

- Focused unit tests green on Play flavor + ThirdParty compile green: `PushToTalkTranscriptMergerTest` (ordering, punctuation/no-doubling, locale punctuation, partial dedupe, empty holds), `PushToTalkRecognitionLadderTest` (descend-only selection, API gating), `TalkModeManagerTest` Robolectric regressions (segment-during-release accumulates without ending the wait; end-of-session completes it; 1.2 s late terminal final is not truncated; rapid re-press: hold A returns its transcript, hold B starts clean; cancellation mid-release clears state and next begin starts immediately).
- `:app:ktlintCheck` green; `git diff --check` clean.
- Structured autoreview: eight rounds; seven accepted findings fixed across the capture/release lifecycle (late-final truncation, raw-rung retry loop, non-terminal segment completion, re-press race, ASCII punctuation corruption, ignored-audio-source hot mic, partial cancellation teardown); final round clean — "fallback ladder, transcript accumulation, release draining, callback isolation, and audio-resource cleanup are internally consistent."
- Live device verification (real microphone/recognizer) planned before landing; not possible in the build environment.
